- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 30-day forecasts start above true values).
- Forecasts show upward bias after sharp price spikes (e.g., after 70+ values, model continues rising while true values often dip or stabilize).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion after high peaks — forecasts remain elevated longer than actual prices.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits “overshoot” behavior after price corrections — forecasts overshoot true values after a sharp drop, then gradually correct.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to reflect volatility or sudden reversals in true price data.
- Model underestimates volatility in early periods (e.g., after a spike, true prices often rebound faster than forecast suggests).
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the short term — especially when true prices show strong downward momentum.
